strings.name: Malala Yousafzai
strings.role: Education advocate · Nobel Peace Prize laureate
strings.summary: Born in Pakistan’s Swat region, Malala Yousafzai documented girls’ exclusion from school under Taliban rule as a child. After surviving a shooting in 2012, she continued advocating education rights, co-founded Malala Fund with her father and shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Kailash Satyarthi. She graduated from Oxford and promotes safe, free education for girls through speeches, funding and writing.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable early life, education and career transitions; checked through 13 November 2026, not a complete news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Has long advocated girls’ right to education and received the Nobel Peace Prize, advancing educational opportunity and gender equality through international public activities.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Philosophy, Politics and Economics, University of Oxford; graduated in 2020
strings.highlights.h1.title: Girls’ education advocacy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Co-founded Malala Fund with her father, supporting girls’ secondary education through grants and public advocacy.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Nobel Peace Prize
strings.highlights.h2.text: Shared the 2014 Peace Prize with Kailash Satyarthi, becoming the youngest Nobel laureate.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Education World Forum address
strings.timeline.t1.text: Spoke at the Education World Forum about how funding cuts and policy delays affect children.
strings.timeline.t2.title: New memoir
strings.timeline.t2.text: Published Finding My Way, reflecting on growing up in public, mental health and personal life.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Oxford graduation
strings.timeline.t3.text: Completed Philosophy, Politics and Economics at Oxford while continuing education advocacy.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Shared Nobel Peace Prize
strings.timeline.t4.text: Received the Nobel Peace Prize jointly with Indian children’s rights advocate Kailash Satyarthi.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Fund and United Nations speech
strings.timeline.t5.text: Co-founded Malala Fund with her father and addressed the United Nations on education rights on her sixteenth birthday.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Survived an attack
strings.timeline.t6.text: Shot by a Taliban gunman on her journey home from school; treated in Britain and continued advocating girls’ education.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Diary of school restrictions
strings.timeline.t7.text: Wrote a BBC Urdu diary under a pseudonym about life under Taliban restrictions on girls’ schooling in Swat.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Mingora childhood
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Mingora in Pakistan’s Swat region; her father ran a school and supported her education.
